$comment: The frozen demonstration dataset: four beats, each with two interchangeable tickets, and the
authored answers that make them land where they are meant to land.
Every ticket declares the clause it is written to fire and what the retrieval is expected to
return for it, and both claims are CHECKED rather than asserted:
test_TRIAGE_demo_dataset_is_authored_for_its_beats runs each authored envelope through the
strict validator and each ticket through the published rule at ALL THREE stages — the record,
the triage and the draft — and fails the build if the reason that survives the precedence is
not the one named here. It evaluates the complete rule of eight clauses; evaluating seven of
them was enough while nothing could produce the eighth, and it would now be a test that stayed
green while the demonstration produced a different verdict in front of the people it was
written for.
Two tickets per beat because a rehearsal needs a second attempt. They are different tickets and
not one ticket twice: the chokepoint's cache is keyed on an input digest that carries the ticket
identifier, so re-running the same ticket is a cache hit — free, reproducible, and NOT a fresh
call. Re-running its twin is a real call. Both are useful and they answer different questions.
created_at is not in this file. seed/demo_load.mjs stamps it at load time, because the SLA
clause is a fact about the clock: a dataset with a fixed timestamp escalates every one of its
tickets on SLA the moment it is a day old, before any model is asked, and the beat that was
supposed to show triage shows a breach instead.
The organisation, account and customer identifiers are the ones seed/orgs.sql fixes, and the
knowledge base each beat is retrieved against is the one seed/orgs.sql seeds.

tickets.subject: Invoice wrong again and payment is now frozen
tickets.body: Our monthly invoice has been wrong for the third quarter running and nobody has come back to us. Finance has frozen payment on the whole account and I am the one explaining it upstairs every week. I need someone who can fix the billing record itself, not another apology.

intended.why: A premium account at severity 3 satisfies the TIER clause too. The intra-stage order is CONF, SENT, TIER, so the answer is authored with a confidence well above the floor and a sentiment below the threshold: CONF cannot fire, SENT fires first, and TIER never gets asked. The reason stored is the one about the customer, which is the one a supervisor can act on. The retrieval expectation is null because the ticket escalates at the triage stage and the drafting cycle never runs for it.

tickets.subject: Same billing error, fourth month, no answer
tickets.body: This is the fourth month in a row that the seat count on our bill does not match what we signed for. Two people have promised a call back and neither has happened. I have run out of patience explaining the same thing to a new person every time.

intended.why: The twin of variant A, written differently so that its digest, and therefore its cache key, is its own.

tickets.subject: Which plan covers a second export destination
tickets.body: We currently export the nightly file to one destination and would like to add a second one for our warehouse team. Could you tell me which plan covers that and whether it changes our monthly total?

intended.why: The beat that shows the whole cycle working: a standard account, a calm enquiry, a confident triage, two articles retrieved from Northwind's own corpus, a reply that cites both, and a validator that agrees. It lands in AWAITING_AGENT with grounded = true, which is the evidence US-03 closes on. Before this increment seeded an article about exports into THIS organisation, the same ticket would have retrieved nothing and escalated on a knowledge gap — the demonstration would have broken not because of what was added but because of what was switched on.

tickets.subject: Can we schedule the nightly job an hour later
tickets.body: Our nightly job currently starts at midnight and we would prefer it to start at one in the morning so it does not overlap with our own batch. Is that something we can change ourselves or do you need to do it?

intended.why: The twin of variant A. Its authored reply cites one of the two retrieved articles and not both, which is legitimate and is worth having in the dataset: a draft must cite what it stands on, not everything it was shown.

tickets.subject: Passing this to our solicitors
tickets.body: We have asked twice for the duplicate charges to be corrected and nothing has moved. Our solicitors have the file now and will be in touch about breach of contract if this is not resolved this week.

intended.why: The deterministic matcher raises the legal flag from the ticket's own record, so the rule fires at the record stage and the ticket escalates WITHOUT a model call. No fixture is authored for it, because the provider is never reached: the ledger stays empty for this ticket and its triage columns stay null, which is the honest picture of an escalation nobody had to pay for.

tickets.subject: Formal complaint about the last two invoices
tickets.body: I would like to raise a formal complaint about the handling of our last two invoices. We were told the correction had been applied and it has not been, and I would like that on record.

intended.why: The twin of variant A, raising the complaint flag instead of the legal one. Same beat, same code, a different written rule underneath it.

tickets.subject: Who is able to view the audit trail for a shipment
tickets.body: A supervisor asked whether the audit trail attached to a shipment is visible to everybody in the workspace or only to whoever raised it. We want to understand the visibility rules first.

intended.why: The beat this increment exists for, and it is authored in NORTHWIND on purpose. Northwind is a standard-tier account, so premium_high_severity cannot fire whatever severity the triage assigns — on the premium tenant a severity-3 answer would escalate on TIER and the ticket would never reach the drafting cycle at all, and the beat would demonstrate the wrong thing while looking correct. The triage is pinned calm — severity 2, sentiment inside [-0.20, +0.30], confidence well above the floor, English, no policy word anywhere in it — so that EXACTLY ONE clause fires and it is the knowledge gap. The retrieval returns zero lexical matches against Northwind's corpus at kb-2026-08-01, no model is asked to draft anything, and the ticket goes to a person having cost nothing.

tickets.subject: How long is an archived shipment kept before it disappears
tickets.body: Somebody on my desk archived a shipment last week and today they cannot find it anywhere. We would like to know how long an archived record stays visible and whether a supervisor can bring it back.

intended.why: The twin of variant A, and the one a rehearsal uses for the second run: a re-run of variant A is a cache hit and costs nothing, which is a useful thing to show and a different thing from a fresh call.

triage_fixtures.match: one destination and would like to add a second
audit trail attached to a shipment

$draft_comment: The authored replies for the one beat that reaches the drafting agent.
They are authored rather than derived because the derived answer, while provably grounded, is a
stitched-together thing that reads like a fixture; a demonstration shows a reply a person could
plausibly send. What makes them safe to author is that they are checked the same way every other
draft is: each one must share a run of consecutive words with every source it cites, and must
not reproduce a long passage from a source it does not cite. An authored reply that stopped
satisfying those would fail the cycle rather than quietly pass it.
No entry is authored for the knowledge-gap beat, and that is the beat: the retrieval returns
nothing, so the drafting agent is never asked.

draft.text: Thanks for getting in touch. A plan covers a fixed number of export destinations, so adding a further destination for a second team is a plan change and it alters the monthly total. We confirm the new figure in writing before it takes effect. If you would also like the run itself to move, the nightly export window can be moved by an account owner from the scheduling screen.

draft_fixtures.match: so it does not overlap with our own batch

draft.text: Thanks for getting in touch. The nightly export window can be moved by an account owner from the scheduling screen, so this is a change you can make yourselves. Moving it later avoids an overlap with a batch that starts at midnight, and the new time applies from the following night.
